chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muammar ibn Khallad who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Abu al-Khattab corrupted the people of Kufa, so they ceased to pray the Maghrib prayer until the redness of the sky (shafaq) disappeared, and that delay was not appropriate except for the traveler or the person with an excuse. He also said: A man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: How did it happen that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said about Abu al-Khattab what he said [initially], and then the decree of disassociation (bara'ah) came regarding him? So he said to him: Was it only for Abu Abdillah to appoint [someone] but not to depose [him]?

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: Abu al-Khattab, a prominent deputy of the Imams
key_terms.الشَّفَق: The twilight glow, the redness in the sky after sunset
key_terms.الْبَرَاءَةُ: Disassociation or declaration of innocence from a person

ai.seo_question: Why did the people of Kufa delay Maghrib prayer and how did the Imam explain the change in status of Abu al-Khattab?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kadhim (Abu al-Hasan) highlights how Abu al-Khattab’s deviation led the people of Kufa to erroneously delay the Maghrib prayer until the disappearance of the twilight glow (shafaq), a concession originally reserved only for travelers or the ill. He further elucidates the theological principle of 'al-istidraj' or gradual disassociation by affirming that the Imam possesses the inherent authority to both appoint and dismiss his deputies, thereby resolving the apparent contradiction between initial praise and subsequent disassociation (bara'ah).
